item.title: eto — Tuesday, September 29, 2026
item.description: The Tuesday, September 29, 2026 edition: 2 stories, each one event told through outlets that disagree.
item.content:encoded:
Markets

  • S&P 500 7683.69 ▼ -59.72 since last edition
  • S&P/TSX 35489.86 ▼ -311.03 since last edition
  • USD/CAD 1.4168 ▲ +0 since last edition
  • Bank of Canada overnight rate 2.25

Business news

  • Euna Procurement’s Marketplace & Invoicing Modules Earn TX-RAMP Level 2 Certification, Meeting Texas Security Requirements for Cloud Services — Financial Post · Euna Procurement’s Marketplace and Invoicing modules achieve TX-RAMP Level 2 certification, meeting Texas security requirements for cloud services processing confidential data.
  • Wood Mackenzie: Europe’s Power Sector Hits 80% Zero-Carbon Generation by 2030, But Misses Its Own Renewables Target — Financial Post · Europe’s power sector reaches 80% zero-carbon generation by 2030 but falls short of its renewables target, with solar PV at 637 GWac and onshore wind at 346 GW by 2030.
  • Smart Ring Maker Oura Postpones IPO Due to Market ‘Uncertainty’ — Bloomberg · Health and fitness ring-maker Oura Inc. will delay its planned initial public offering on Nasdaq due to uncertainty in the market for first time offerings.
  • Credit Card Application Fraud Climbs as Identity Thieves Disproportionately Target Canadians Aged 56 to 65 — Financial Post
  • Nespresso and Swarovski Invite You to Make Every Coffee Moment Shine — Financial Post
  • Oura postpones IPO, citing market uncertainty: markets live — MarketWatch
  • Cash Gold Market Booms in India as High Prices and Taxes Bite — Bloomberg · Exorbitantly high gold prices and steep taxes are driving more Indian buyers into under-the-counter cash sales, where bullion and jewelry change hands without invoices that can be traced by authorities.
  • Matthew Lau: Ontario’s fiscal news is bad all around — Financial Post · Yes, last year's deficit was lower than budgeted but the improvement was mainly due to luck and the budgeted deficit was too high by far
  • Bjorn Lomborg: The Great Barrier Reef refuses to die on schedule — Financial Post · Experts have been predicting its imminent demise for 20 years, but in terms of coral cover, the past five years were the best on record
  • Ford says Ontario willing to bankroll ‘nation-building’ pipeline from Alberta to Sarnia — Financial Post · Ontario's premier later said he expects outside investors to help finance the proposed Northern Shield pipeline which would move up to 500,000 barrels per day

The brief ends here.

Are London's bridges really falling down? Harry Black explains. (Source: Bloomberg)
